items.body: Review by OlyaBeginner — Listening to this album was not simply about hearing music ? it was a journey through emotions, images, and inner states. Though I am not an expert in this genre, I approached each composition with openness, letting the sounds speak to my feelings and imagination. What follows is a personal reflection on the atmosphere and emotions each piece evoked in me.1) The Tragedy of the Ancient Spring. A sense of a new beginning arises. Maybe it's about a new period of life or rethinking life, which appears in a bright light. The sound of greatness and heritage fills the soul. Next, the listener hears a transition into a piano section, which creates the feeling of action and gradual movement. Afterward, a development into faster, more dynamic sound appears, and a sense of potential and growth is felt. Finally, the composition ends with a mysterious and hypnotic feeling.2) Captivated. The beginning immediately captures attention. Sleeping or dreaming, the listener seems to awaken from hypnosis. The image of someone inspired arises. He decides to take action in order to get his object of desire. There's a sense of enthusiasm and great effort to handle one's obsession, its nearness evokes a sense of greatness. But there is a confusion and perhaps disappointment, which are the finishing part. Realization and fatigue fill the ending of the composition.3) Target. A gradual deepening into something mysterious is replaced with soft sounds that prepare the listener for the next part. Its speed and instability induce the feeling of torments of the soul. Uncertainty creates a motive for searching the solution. Harsh sounds make a listener feel on alert, nudging the listener to keep searching and moving forward.4) Teach Me Your Statutes. This composition can make you feel deeply sad. The listener experiences mutual misunderstanding, disappointment, and desperation while listening to this. Though these are often seen as negative feelings, the strength and beauty of them cannot go unnoticed. In the second part, there is development. Transition to hardly notable sounds and thrill create the tension and anxious atmosphere. Perhaps the beginnings of love or commitment are the most fitting context to experience this feeling.5) Loneliness-Bringing Power.The composition starts gradually, preparing the listener for something important. The slow melody creates a comforting atmosphere. It transitions into something unknown and challenging ? perhaps loneliness. It flows into taking on a challenge and a way to achieve something meaningful, bringing new discoveries and experiences. The denouement brings a sense of joy and happiness.6) Three Sunny Light Power. The beginning immerses the listener and suggests a great power. As it builds up, the feelings of enthusiasm and inspiration arise. It can be determination to create and live. It motivates to enjoy life and to be in the moment. This part ends with the sound of bells. The bells give a final polish to what has been achieved and bring the feeling of satisfaction.7) Resilience. The soft sounds gently awaken the listener in the beginning of the composition. The atmosphere conveys calm, stability, and peace of mind. Subtle hints of mystery transit the listener to loading into realization and meaning. It then gives way to a graceful finale. The feeling of probable resilience can inspire confidence and a quiet sense of satisfaction.8) Silence Is Waiting. It starts in a similar way to the previous composition. There is a hypnotic quality here as well. It creates a perfect atmosphere to meditate and clear thoughts. A sense of peace comes over the listener. The cosmic sounds evoke space, making the listener feel weightless and far removed from earthly concerns.Each composition on the album felt like a chapter in an emotional and spiritual narrative ? sometimes uplifting, sometimes sorrowful, but always sincere. This album offers more than sound; it offers space for reflection, imagination, and inner movement.

Hard work and inspiration. Perseverance, courage and hard work, goal setting helps. The main thing is to see what you are doing it for.Jungle Waltz. Beautiful, mysterious game and playfulness. It seems that tropical animals are walking and playing around. Mystery, tension take place at the end accompanying a final battle the main wild characters participate in.The Hidden Man of the Heart. Virtue, hope, rise, the path to achieving the goal come up while listening to this composition.Lavoro D'amore. Relationships can be difficult. If you want to build relationships you need to put a lot of effort. You have to try your best to go through quarrels, misunderstandings, anger, resentment. Then comes relief, revival, a new stage of the relationships.Forbearing One Another in Love. Seems like this composition reflects the stages of relationships. Fleeting glances, sympathy. Love. Two clarified each other. It started out hard. Misunderstanding. They were spinning in the stream. Everything is great. Very beautiful, fairy tale. Storm, fake and condescend, work on relationships. Relief has come.Recovery. Vanity and care are replaced by joy and enjoyment of life, improving the internal state and finding peace.Ascension of hope. It embraces feelings of beauty, love, kindness, lightness, sublimity, flight, hope.Passing winter. Light sadness, melancholy, fear and mystery change to hope and enlightenment, excitement, with a feeling of peace and awareness that everything is going as usual. Magical and bright feelings, beauty and sadness occur.Ending. The road and the work, enjoying the result and the experience that was gained.Mother of all rain. The peace and joy that we experience in good times, in sunny weather, the laconically and unexpectedly change to the charming and immersing. You feel the atmosphere of strength, struggle and work that we experience in difficult times or in rainy weather. You go through difficulties and move on.Passing over. Boiling and seething change to the peace. Then it changes immediately to the mystery. You continue the path, with new experience.

items.body: Review by Stefano61 — There is a particular kind of return that has nothing to do with nostalgia and everything to do with stubbornness.Opus Avantra were born in the Veneto in the early seventies out of an idea rather than a line-up: AVANguardia and TRAdizione, avant-garde and tradition, welded into a single word by the soprano Donella Del Monaco, the pianist and composer Alfredo Tisocco, the philosopher Giorgio Bisotto and the producer Renato Marengo. Their 1974 debut, universally known as Introspezione, remains one of the strangest objects in the entire Italian catalogue of that decade, a record that belongs to progressive rock mostly because nobody could think where else to file it, and which earned the group a place on the Nurse With Wound list among the true outsiders of European music.Lord Cromwell Plays Suite For Seven Vices followed in 1975, then long silences broken by Strata in 1989, Lyrics in 1995, and Venetia et Anima in 2003. Sixteen years later, on the fourteenth of January 2019, Rosa Rosae appeared, produced once again by Renato Marengo, the same man who had produced the debut forty five years earlier, under the artistic direction of Tisocco. Whatever else it is, it is a circle closing.The record is credited to Donella Del Monaco, Paolo Troncon and the Opus Avantra Ensemble, and that order of names is accurate. Del Monaco writes all the texts and sings them, moving between Latin, Italian and French with a delivery that comes from the conservatory and from a family where the surname Del Monaco meant something before she ever recorded a note. Troncon composes, arranges and directs, and his training is classical and contemporary rather than rock: he writes in polyrhythmic and contrapuntal forms rather than in verses and choruses, which is precisely why this is not a pop record wearing a costume.The ensemble is Mauro Martello on flutes, saxophones and duduk, Laura Balbinot on cello, Andrea De Nardi on keyboards and Giorgio Cedolin on drums, expanded by accordions, a second cello, tenor saxophones and percussion. The guest list reads like a summit of the Italian seventies: Tony Esposito, who had already played on the 1974 debut, Lino Vairetti of Osanna, Jenny Sorrenti of Saint Just, and Alberto Radius of Formula 3, whose contribution here now carries an unintended weight, since he died in February 2023.The theme is the rose and therefore love, declined between sacred and profane, devotion and desire, with the two poles deliberately confused and sometimes inverted. It is a concept album in the old and serious sense of the term, not a suite with a title stuck on afterwards.A word on sequencing, because it matters. The 2019 CD ran nine pieces and opened with the accordion led lyricism of Nuvole Bianche. The later vinyl edition carries eleven, fully resequenced, adding the previously unreleased L'Angelo Caduto, restoring Aurea Lyra in its original version rather than the CD reworking, and bringing Sceleratus back as a closing reprise. That order opens with the darkest music on the record and holds the warmth in reserve, which strikes me as the truer shape of the work.The track-by-track below follows the vinyl sequence.- Sceleratus: the severest thing here, sung in Latin, with Lino Vairetti's powerful Mediterranean baritone answering Del Monaco line for line. Exorcism and mysticism circling each other. As an opening statement it warns you immediately that this will not be comfortable listening.- Mandala: an instrumental in all but atmosphere, built on the interlocking percussion of Tony Esposito and Gabriele Bruzzolo over Troncon's piano, with Andrea Martin's tenor saxophone tracing long lines above. The most openly rhythmic piece on the album, and the clearest link back to the debut.- Aurea Lyra (original version): piano by Dimitri Romano, accordion, cello and percussion, a chamber ensemble rather than a band. The original reading is drier and less upholstered than the one issued on CD, and it gains from that.- Pi Greco: the shortest and most abstract passage, a piece of pure construction whose title tells you everything about the intention. It functions as a hinge rather than a destination.- Rosa Rosae: the title track, and the centre of gravity. Tenor saxophone, accordion, cello and piano weave around Del Monaco's voice in what is closest here to a genuine song, though the counterpoint never relaxes into accompaniment. The rose as flower and as rosary, both at once.- L'Angelo Caduto: the previously unreleased piece, and no mere appendix. The fallen angel is the natural counterpart to the diabolic material of Sceleratus, and it sits squarely inside the concerns of the record rather than beside them. Its absence from the CD now feels like an omission.- Nuvole Bianche: the accordion of Mirko Satto and Troncon's piano, the most immediately beautiful thing on the album and the piece that once opened it. Placed here, deep into the second side, it arrives as relief rather than as invitation, which suits it better.- Cyrcles: Alberto Radius plugs in and plays, unmistakably, with that liquid seventies tone set against Tommaso Troncon's tenor saxophone. A deliberate homage to the decade the group came from, and now an elegy as well.- Vento Del Nord: written by Del Monaco with Mauro Martello, and the one duet on the record, with Jenny Sorrenti. Two voices that could easily have fought each other and instead lean together. Quietly the most moving few minutes here.- Ineffabile Realt�: Troncon alone at the piano. After everything that has preceded it, the austerity feels earned rather than imposed.- Sceleratus (Reprise): the Latin returns, briefly, and the door closes on the same shadow it opened with.Rosa Rosae asks something of the listener, and it does not pretend otherwise. Those who come to Opus Avantra hoping for the corrosive weirdness of Introspezione will find this more measured, more written, more willing to be beautiful; the fracture lines of 1974 have been smoothed by fifty years of thinking about the same problem. There are moments where the chamber writing verges on the decorous, and the abstract interludes will lose the impatient.Yet the ambition is intact and entirely unfashionable: a group that has spent half a century refusing to choose between the conservatory and the rock stage, still refusing, still finding new ways to hold the two apart without letting either win. Del Monaco's voice has darkened and gained gravity, Troncon's writing gives it architecture worthy of it, and the guests are used as colours rather than as selling points.This is a late chapter, and it knows it, but it is a rich one and it belongs on the shelf beside the records that made the name. An excellent album from a band that never learned how to be ordinary.My rating: 4/5.Bassano del Grappa (Italy), August 2026

items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 980Porcupine Tree is an English progressive rock band that was formed in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire. The band consists of a mix of prog rock, psych rock, avant-garde experimentalism and heavy metal. Despite this, Wilson doesn't have the same opinion. He mentions that Porcupine Tree's music is very simple, without complex elements. The complexity is in the production, in the way the albums are constructed. His first recordings "On The Sunday Of Life..." released in 1992 and "Up The Downstair" released in 1993, contain Wilson's first compositions, reminiscent of the cosmic rock of old glories like Pink Floyd and Eloy, but also resemble of the ambient rock from some contemporary bands like Ozric Tentacles. Wilson played all the instruments and did the drum programming. In addition, he invited some guest musicians to complete the picture on those works. By recording his acclaimed third album "The Sky Moves Sideways" released in 1995, which is the subject of this review, Wilson makes Porcupine Tree a true band. The new group received acclaim from critics around the world who describe the band as "The Pink Floyd of the new century".So, "The Sky Moves Sideways" is the third studio album of Porcupine Tree that was released in 1995. The line up on "The Sky Moves Sideways" is Steven Wilson (vocals, electric and acoustic guitars, bass guitar, keyboards, flute, tapes and programming), Richard Barbieri (keyboards and electronics), Colin Edwin (bass and double bass guitars) and Chris Maitland (drums and percussion). "The Sky Moves Sideways" had also the participation of Suzanne Barbieri (vocals), Theo Travis (flute), Gavin Harrison (drums overdubs) and Rick Edwards (percussion), all as guest musicians.After some success achieved with their previous albums, Wilson decided it was time for the band to hit the road, but for that he would have to have full-time musicians around. So he recruited the talented Richard Barbieri, Colin Edwin and Chris Maitland. Originally, the album should have been released as a single track, an epic work of about 50-minutes. However, this version was never finished, but divided into two parts which added up to about 36-minutes that begin and end the album, following an idea similar to that of Pink Floyd in "Wish You Were Here", with "Shine On You Crazy Diamond". In general, "The Sky Moves Sideways" walks in the footsteps of Pink Floyd, like no other work of the band, with a modern approach. With this work, the band manages to create a great album that picks up the tempo at the right places with rocky excursions where no boredom is and there's always something to discover even after many runs.The original version of "The Sky Moves Sideways" has six tracks. As I mentioned above, the title track suite is divided in two parts, opening and closing the original album. At its core, it was constructed and recorded alone by Wilson, but had overdubs by each of the three new members of the band, although Maitland didn't replace the drum machine, but only played the congas. The shortest recordings filling the middle of the album remained completely recorded solo. The piece is made in the best space rock style with the atmospheric sounds of Pink Floyd. The main passages are based on improvisations. Even so, the moods and sections are always well structured, making the music develop in an involving and dynamic way. As the suite winds toward its conclusion, some of the earlier instrumental themes are reprised. This suite is a masterpiece. "Dislocated Day" with its Oriental mood and melody is an excellent and very dark song, with a strong and emotive guitar riff that glides through the song in a very solid way. Solid are also the other instruments that energize the music with the maximum force. "The Moon Touches Your Shoulder" is a kind of an introspective ballad. It features beautiful acoustic guitar chords surrounded by lush keyboards and Wilson's airy vocals. The second half of the track is when things get more intense. Layers of sound introduce a kind of a guitar cacophony that settles down and carries us to the next track. "Prepare Yourself" is a very short instrumental featuring a good guitar work over an atmospheric keyboard and subtle bass drum beats. "Moonloop" seems to have been released in countless versions and lengths. It was created on completely different principles than the rest of the album. In the absence of Barbieri, and with the percussionist Edwards, the band entered the studio to record an improvisation eventually completing the repertoire of the album. It comes a bit close to the sound of the central piece with its expansive space rock passages.Conclusion: "The Sky Moves Sideways" is one of the albums to indicate to someone who doesn't know the band's work yet. On it, they actually performed as a band for the first time. The album represents a turning point in the band's work. Overall, "The Sky Moves Sideways" is an excellent example of the new psychedelic music style. This is probably, for me, the most atmospheric Porcupine Tree's album. "The Sky Moves Sideways" has a lot of moody, hypnotic and deep musical atmospheres. This is really an entertaining journey of discovery through Wilson's cosmos of sound. "The Sky Moves Sideways" is undoubtedly a masterpiece where each song is well arranged, well performed and well written.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)

items.body: Review by maxsmusic — After such a long stretch of no new music, it was good to see this band produce a new record. They waited so long because they wanted to make sure they really had something worthwhile to say. They are all great writers and have many songs to choose from. Ty puts out solo records and the Jelly Jam. Jerry has two really good solo albums and Dug is extremely prolific in so many bands, solo and with others. However, there is something special when these three guys collaborate together. Their back catalogue has some real gems and they always try not to repeat themselves. The last three studio albums are very good and they are each very unique. Three Sides of One is reflective on growing older, technology and the spiritual world. Excellent work.

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — The third studio album from Norwegian band Seven Impale is definitely one of the long-awaitedprogressive rock releases of the decade, as it arrives seven years after their previous work'Contrapasso'. Seven Impale is a six-piece band that plays a pretty complex and theatrical style ofprogressive rock - their sound is heavily informed by the avant-garde rock scene as much as it is byclassic prog acts like Crimson and Van der Graaf. One could say their music is wilder than �nglag�rdand Ankedoten, yet it is no less sophisticated than the output of bands like Shamblemaths or Birdsand Buildings. Ideally, Seven Impale play a fusion-inspired modern rendition of retro prog; one thatis playful and dense, but also compositionally astute. And this is precisely what I admire abouttheir third album 'Summit' - a relentless record made up of four epics replete with tremendousmusical ideas, downright anxious instrumental sections, an interesting predisposition to dissonance,and an infectious energy.The titles of the four tracks suggest a mythological thread that underpins the concept of thisrecord. The epic nature of the music is then certainly befitting for such a conceptual thread, asthe four large pieces of heavy avant-prog deliver an in-your-face technicality mixed up with theband's pleasantly theatrical delivery. Lots of saxes and analog synths appear on this album, whichhas righteously reminded some listeners of Wobbler. But unlike their compatriots, Seven Impaleincorporate gnarly guitar riffs into their music, bringing in an almost sludgy feel to the heaviertracks. And this album certainly does not shy away from displaying pounding sections of heavy prog.All four compositions on 'Summit' are around the ten-minute mark, and their usual structure involvesan instrumental intro, followed by a swift transition into the main verse (and this is where themore intense or unusual ideas enter), leading up to a chorus that could be anything from cerebraland anthemic to crazy and surreal, after which an extended instrumental section brings thatexplosion of hectic ideas, complex interplay between the different instruments, and an overalleccentric feel. I cannot decide if I like 'Hunter' or 'Hydra' more, but the 13-minute album closer'Sisyphus' is up there with the best material on 'Summit', which to me is nothing short of astunning album. Highly recommended contemporary jazz-prog.

items.body: Review by Stefano61 — Forty six years passed between the celebrated 1972 debut of Reale Accademia di Musica and this second album, one of the longest gaps between two releases in the history of Italian rock.Guitarist Pericle Sponzilli, the sole returning member from the original lineup, reactivated the name in 2018 after being invited in September 2014 by organizer Guido Bellachioma to perform at the Progressivamente Free Festival alongside old companions from Fholks and acquaintances such as l'Uovo di Colombo, la Raccomandata con Ricevuta di Ritorno and Saint Just.Sponzilli took the decision partly because, in the intervening decades, other formations had used the historic Reale Accademia di Musica name for records that, in his view, did not represent the group's real legacy; Angeli Mutanti was conceived as what he considered the true second album of the band.Around him he assembled Fabio Liberatori, formerly of Stadio and a longtime collaborator of Lucio Dalla, on piano and keyboards, Erika Savastani, from Deserto Rosso, on vocals, Fabio Fraschini on bass, and Andy Bartolucci on drums, with guest guitarists Gianfranco Coletta, Nicola Di Staso and Fernando Fera contributing to individual tracks.Produced by Sponzilli and Liberatori themselves and released on the twenty eighth of February 2018 through M.P. & Records, in CD and in a limited edition of 300 white vinyl copies, the album carries artwork by Daniele Massimi built around a cover painting by Luciano Regoli, singer of La Raccomandata con Ricevuta di Ritorno, deliberately reviving the band's original 1972 logo while signalling a more contemporary sound.That contemporary sound is the record's defining choice. Angeli Mutanti bears almost no resemblance to the pastoral, mellotron soaked symphonic rock of the 1972 original. It favors instead compact, melody driven songwriting, warm ballads and soft rock textures, carried by the constant interplay between Sponzilli's raspy, characterful voice and Savastani's soulful, soaring one.Progressive elements surface less as extended instrumental workouts than as harmonic and structural details tucked inside otherwise accessible songs: unusual time signatures, brief but unmistakable echoes of Genesis, and orchestral flourishes that recall the golden age of Italian symphonic rock without ever trying to replicate it outright.The opening title track, Angeli Mutanti (Mutant angels), conjures in music and words a set of strange, nameless creatures that fly without wings or feathers, emotionally charged yet harmless, invisible demons without any plan. Musically it is a deceptively simple pop rock tune, lifted by light Hammond organ touches and unhurried, tasty guitar soloing.Alba (Dawn) follows in 5/4 time, its Genesis influenced writing plain to hear. The lyrics describe a metaphorical search for the rising sun and for a better day beyond time and space, a way out of a dark landscape built on lies, set against a bluesy tension and cold, Neo Prog style synthesizers.Johnny e Adele, a melancholic ballad featuring guest guitarist Gianfranco Coletta, paints a beautiful girl dancing on the beach to the notes of a guitar, and the dreams of the guitarist who loves her, colored throughout by warm Moog textures.Cosa nascondono le nuvole (What the clouds hide), with Nicola Di Staso guesting on guitar, opens with a knowing, cryptic echo of Genesis' Hairless Heart before settling into a dreamy, sleek pop rock groove that closes on a Mellotron laced outro clearly indebted to PFM, its words reaching toward far horizons.The Beat Goes On (come la canzone), featuring Fernando Fera on electric guitar, is the album's most straightforward moment, an elegant ballad built on soft, chiming guitar lines.Tempo (Time) turns toward more overtly progressive territory within the record's song based frame, its title alone signalling the preoccupation with time, memory and change that runs beneath even the album's most accessible melodies.A dritta San Salvador keeps the same balance of refined songwriting and understated instrumental interplay that defines the album's midsection, and has been singled out by Italian critics, alongside Io sono qui, Johnny e Adele, Cosa nascondono le nuvole and Tempo, for the sophistication of its trame, its narrative and musical weave.Una sola immagine (A single image), included only on the CD edition, stands apart for its authorship: the lyrics were written not by Sponzilli but by Nada Malanima, the celebrated Italian singer songwriter, lending the song a distinct voice within the album's otherwise unified lyrical perspective.Io sono qui (I am here), introduced by an almost solemn marching rhythm, is full of positive energy and describes an experience of daily rebirth guided by a sensei, a spiritual master whose words function like a chant to be followed in the morning light.The closing instrumental, La pista e il miraggio (The track and the mirage), mixes vintage sounds with exotic, almost cinematic atmospheres, arriving at symphonic passages that sit somewhere between PFM and Pink Floyd, and sending the album out on its most overtly progressive note.Angeli Mutanti was warmly received both in Italy and abroad, in Latin America, Japan, Korea, Canada and the Netherlands, and convinced even critics who had followed the historic Reale Accademia di Musica since the seventies, though a handful of more nostalgic voices wished for longer, more overtly progressive arrangements. Heard today, that same compactness feels less like a limitation and more like a deliberate choice.My judgment: 4 out of 5.Angeli Mutanti succeeds precisely because it does not try to be a sequel to the 1972 album in anything but name and spirit. It is instead a confident, contemporary record built on strong songwriting, a well balanced male and female vocal partnership, and just enough progressive character, in its harmonies, its guest guitar work, its unexpected time signatures, to remind the listener exactly which tradition it comes from.For anyone building a collection around the Italian progressive rock scene and its long, often improbable afterlives, this is a genuinely excellent addition, and a fitting first chapter to the story that Sponzilli would go on to continue four years later with Lame di Luce.

items.body: Review by Molloy — The new album by Compassionizer, "The Fellowship of the Mystery", continues Ivan Rozmainsky and histeam's bold experiments in musical artistry. As with the band's previous works, biblical referencesin the track titles provide the the album with structural cohesion and profound meaning. The albumopens with the evocative piece �To Abound and To Suffer Need", an emotional journey through shiftingmoods that oscillate between hope and despair, only to return triumphantly to hope. This powerfulinterplay of feelings sets the tone for the entire album. The second track, "Avenge Not Yourselves",immerses listeners in an atmosphere of austere contemplation. Its slow, meditative melodies inviteintrospection, preparing the audience for the album's subsequent explorations. This meditationseamlessly transitions into "To Direct Your Hearts into Love", a piece characterized by itssoothing, tranquil tones. As one of the album's standout gems, it radiates warmth and evokes a senseof gentle elevation. Among the most memorable tracks is "I Feel Shine of the Day", inspired by apoem by Ekaterina Vorotnikova. This bright and enchanting composition conjures an almost fairy-tale-like atmosphere, reminiscent of a dialogue between mythical beings?perhaps a fairy and a unicorn. Itbeckons listeners to embark on a magical adventure of life, celebrating the beauty and wonder ofexistence. Building on the theme of benevolent and mystical beings, the album explores the conceptof unseen helpers and miraculous saviors. The track "For Them Who Shall be Heirs of Salvation"reflects on the idea of angelic intervention. Its title alludes to the divine mission of beings sentto aid the heirs of salvation. The philosophical centerpiece of the album, "For the InvisibleThings", prompts reflection on the fleeting nature of the visible and the enduring significance ofthe unseen. Through its intricate melodies, the piece suggests that by reaching toward theinvisible, we may touch something eternal and profound. Finally, the titular track, "The Fellowshipof the Mystery", concludes the album triumphantly. It serves as a reflection on the journey ofenlightened souls, celebrating the mystery of existence and the divine threads that connect us all.With its harmonious blend of biblical themes, poetic inspiration, and musical ingenuity, "TheFellowship of the Mystery" takes listeners on a transcendent journey. It invites them to ponder thevisible and the invisible, the fleeting and the eternal, leaving an indelible impression of beautyand depth.

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 'Sylvanite' is a 2003 studio album from Nad Sylvan, a singer and multi-instrumentalist who rose toprominence as the vocalist of Steve Hackett's Genesis Revisited touring band. Sylvan is also knownfor his collaborative work with members of The Flower Kings and Karmakanic as well as for being partof Inside Out Music's artists roster. And while most people recognize him for his recent prog rocksolo albums, very few are actually familiar with his earlier output, which is where we find thefunky pop-rock effort titled 'Sylvanite'. This is a commercially appealing album that exhibits astrong influence from pop artists like Prince and Blondie, and while it is enjoyable because it isaccessible, it is nowhere near the quality and sophistication of Nad Sylvan's prog rock efforts. Bythe way, he plays all the instruments here and is only joined by two female backing vocalists, whichis impressive. Songs that are worth checking out on this release are 'McNamara's Son', 'The GreatestStory Ever Told', 'Yellow Sky', and 'Bitch on Guitar'. Keep in mind that some tracks have a discovibe but play 'Sylvanite' if you want to hear some funky pop-rock and especially if you enjoy NadSylvan's vocals.

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 2026 is the year of surprise-releases, and Boards of Canada definitely surprised their fanbase withthe release of a fifth studio album titled 'Inferno' on May 29, some thirteen years after'Tomorrow's Harvest'. The electronic duo consisting of Mike Sandison and Marcus Eoin has relied oncryptic messaging and atmospheric soundscapes ever since the 1998 release of their game-changing IDMcollection 'Music Has the Right to Children', and while this kind of music has never had a universalappeal in the mainstream, it has an undeniable edge that attracts listeners from variousbackgrounds. Going back to 'Inferno', this album echoes beautifully the darker and nostalgic tonesof earlier BoC albums. Perhaps a reaction to everything surrounding us nowadays, this eighteen-trackcollection expands the sonic palette of the Scottish duo and impresses with impeccable productionand a myriad of contemporary sounds. At its core a bleak-sounding album, however, this cinematic andexpansive release offers several intriguing electronic pieces, while it preserves the enigmaticnature of the duo's classic compositions.And still, no matter how many times I play 'Inferno', one unfavorable aspect of it always resurfaces- the styles and influences covered here can and do feel somewhat scattered. Of course, themasterful embodying of various sounds tends to compensate for the intimidating abundance ofdifferent genres of electronic music featured here, but this is something that underwhelmed mypersonal listening experience. Of the eighteen tracks on 'Inferno', I tend to really enjoy abouthalf of them, mildly appreciate roughly a quarter, and easily skip the rest. For example, 'Prophecyat 1420 MHz' enters with a moving eastern-inspired intro, which is followed by a haunting palette ofsounds that almost has a noir aesthetic to it. This darker aesthetic is then expanded on 'HydrogenHelium Lithium Leviathan', where the synths seemingly feed off each other, and on 'Somewhere RightNow in the Future', which reminds me of a gloomy daydream. 'Blood in the Labyrinth' is another trackexploring this somber atmosphere, and for whatever reason it reminds me of The Cure. At the sametime, the most intriguing pieces on 'Inferno' are the more ominous, occult-ridden tracks like'Father and Son' with its claustrophobic sound design, 'Naraka' and its wonderful tribal vibes, andthe uneasy but meditative piece 'The Word Becomes Flesh'.There are also many ambient-inspired instrumentals as well, and while some of them are lush andspacey, others feel like interludes or simply random entries. 'All Reason Departs' and 'MemoryDeath' are among the fine ones, while tracks like 'Arena Americanada', 'Into the Magic Land', and'You Retreat in Time and Space' strike me as forgettable. Overall, 'Inferno' is an excellentsurprise from Boards of Canada, and an album worthy of praise that offers a mostly alternativerendition of contemporary electronic music.

items.body: Review by kev rowland — I have not previously come across Arnaud Quevedo, but he is a French musician who has been teaching music at the Conservatoire since 2007 and has been performing under his own name since 2020. This live release from Arnaud Quevedo & Friends finds them performing in summer 2025 and features Quevedo (guitar, vocals, keyboards, alto sax) being joined by Noe Russeil (bass, vocals), Hortense Mailhos (drums), Julien Gomila (soprano & baritone saxophones) and Elo�se Baleynaud (lead vocals, keyboards).This is fusion which also contains some Crimson elements, and the band are very tight indeed, and can also be quite heavy at times, which makes for an interesting mix of styles and dynamics. The sax is an integral music as opposed to an afterthought, while the rhythm section certainly set the stage (the bass on this is stunning throughout) and Quevedo is a super guitarist. But, and it was fairly obvious there was a "but" coming, I am not a huge fan of Elo�se Baleynaud. We get quite a lot of scat, and much of her vocals are very much in the jazz vein, yet there are just too many times when she is not quite on point, which is fine when at a concert as people tend to overlook that but when listening to the performance it very much stands out, and in many ways lets down the rest. Her vocals have also been placed slightly to the rear in the mix, so she does not stand out as much as one would expect, and when she is providing backing vocals she seems more confident and at ease.The album is very loose, but also plenty tight, and I know if I was able to see them in concert I would, but whether I will return often to this CD is another matter altogether.

items.body: Prince Alla has been singing roots since the 1970s, and on “Jah Is My Rock” his voice sits over a riddim that came together on the Spanish coast. Born Keith Blake in Kingston in 1950, he made his name with Bertram Brown‘s Freedom Sounds label, cutting “Stone” over a King Tubby dub mix and following it with “Bucket Bottom“. That same open-throated, declamatory delivery runs through this one too, and the title leans on the old Psalm line about God as a rock. The riddim is the work of Hal C, the Alicante producer Mario Coloma, who came up through the Barcelona reggae scene and now runs Piramid Records. He laid the track down at his own studio, then brought in players from across the map to finish it. Karl Wright cut the drums in the United States, Roberto Sánchez handled the backing vocals at his A-Lone Ark Muzik Studio in Santander, and Danny Trees mixed and mastered. It lands as the label’s fourth 7″, a black-vinyl 45 in a full-colour sleeve, with a dub of the rhythm on the flip. items.body: I’M NOT SURE IF THIS WORLD SURVIVES I CAN’T TELL YOU WHAT’S TRUTH OR LIES IT DOESN’T MATTER IF YOU’RE LEFT OR RIGHT WE’RE ALL DEAD UNLESS WE ALL UNITE After more than four decades spent turning political disgust, technological dread, and distorted guitars into blunt-force industrial rock, Ministry is preparing to shut down the machinery. Al Jourgensen has announced that the band’s forthcoming album, Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery), will be its last, bringing one of heavy music’s loudest and most unruly careers to a close on October 30 through Cleopatra Records. The first preview comes with Burned Out, a new single accompanied by a video directed by Joshua Bradford, formerly of Revolting Cocks. The title sounds like both a diagnosis and a resignation letter, which feels appropriate for a band that has spent decades staring directly at American power, institutional rot, religious hypocrisy, corporate greed, and the people who profit from keeping everyone exhausted and furious. Jourgensen has rarely been shy about announcing exactly what he thinks of the world, and Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery) gives him one final album-sized opportunity to unload. The record finds Ministry taking stock of those in charge, the damage they have caused, and whatever possibility remains for people trying to move forward together without surrendering their minds in the process. Jourgensen is equally direct about his decision to end the band. “I’m fucking done,” he says. “I’m proud of what I’ve accomplished. I’m amazed at the path that it’s taken, from With Sympathy to where we’re at today, and all points in between. It’s been quite a ride, but I’m completely at peace with the fact that it’s done. It’s time to herd goats.” It is a characteristically Jourgensen farewell. Ministry’s history has never followed a clean route, moving from the synth-pop framework of With Sympathy toward increasingly abrasive combinations of industrial electronics, metal, punk, samples, drum machines, and political invective. Along the way, the group built a catalogue whose influence spread through alternative rock, industrial metal, electronic music, and nearly every basement club willing to risk its speaker system. Burned Out surveys a planet apparently being administered by arsonists, war profiteers, algorithmic creeps, petty tyrants, and terminally online lunatics, while everybody else stares into the smoke wondering which official lie they are supposed to swallow today. Wars multiply, humanitarian disasters become background noise, the climate cooks, repression spreads, and domestic extremism crawls out of the basement wearing a flag. Beneath all that wreckage sits one stubborn plea: stand together before fear, division, and authoritarian power finish carving us into manageable pieces. The video turns the crisis into a parade of deranged animation, with Uncle Al planted at its center like the last sane man at the end of civilization, coat practically on, ready to abandon the madhouse before somebody asks him to save it. Watch below: Since beginning in 1981, Ministry has released 17 studio albums, 8 live releases, 8 side projects, tours across 5 continents, an autobiography, 2 documentaries, and at least 3 occasions on which Jourgensen received last rites. The survival stories became inseparable from the music, turning the band’s continued existence into a running argument against medical probability and professional caution. Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery) also closes part of the Ministry story by reconnecting Jourgensen with longtime member Paul Barker. Barker appears on the album’s final track, We’re Still Here, marking one last collaboration between two musicians whose work together helped define Ministry’s most widely celebrated period. The album also features Ministry’s current lineup, including guitarists Monte Pittman and Cesar Soto, bassist Paul D’Amour, sampler and synthesizer player John Bechdel, and drummer Pepe Clarke Magaña. Together, they provide the final formation behind a band that has spent 45 years treating complacency as an enemy and volume as a public service. Ministry’s final album, Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery), is out October 30 through Cleopatra Records. Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery) will be available in several formats including vinyl, CD, cassettes and digital, also including several vinyl variants and box sets: Green & Black Splatter LP Silver & Black Splatter LP Coke Bottle Green LP Box Set: Green Splatter LP, Picture LP, 7-inch, CD Box Set: Purple Marble LP, Picture LP, 7-inch, CD Fans can pre-save the digital album HERE and pre-order digital copies HERE, and find a new Ministry merch line HERE. Ministry will bring tracks from Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery) and other classic hits on the road in 2027 with an international goodbye tour. The Goodbye Europe Tour, featuring special guest Die Krupps, begins in April 2027. It will be followed by a full U.S. run, to be announced. European tour dates will include exclusive meet-and-greet opportunities with Al Jourgensen, featuring a photo op, a souvenir laminate pass, a silk-screen poster, and a final European tour coin. Fans can purchase meet-and-greets here. In the meantime, Ministry has a few final U.S. tour dates for 2026, including Chicago’s Salt Shed, the historic Red Rocks in Colorado and appearances at Louder Than Life and Sick New World Texas. Find more info and tickets at MinistryBand.com. items.body: PUREST FORM’s latest single, ANIMAL, opens with electronic menace. A blunt industrial beat stomps into view, guitar slashes scrape across the machinery, and Story Beeson’s voice carries the command of somebody who has already located the emergency exit. The Los Angeles trio wanted “White Zombie meets Underworld,” which sounds on paper like a backstage argument at a 1997 festival, yet the combination proves remarkably natural. Beeson, guitarist and programmer Madi Woodward, and bassist Riley Oikawa-Dahlson bring hardcore discipline to music designed for bodies in motion. ANIMAL pivots between serrated riffs, fractured breakbeats, low-end pressure, and sudden structural swerves, but every turn feels purposeful. The track has muscle, sex, and a mean little grin. Its aggression never becomes gray sludge; there is too much rhythmic wit in the programming, too much snap in the bass, and too much pleasure in the collision between metal weight and acid-house momentum. There is also a refreshing lack of genre etiquette here; stylistic boundaries are treated as petty municipal ordinances, useful mainly for telling dull people where to stand, then barrel through them with the cheerful confidence of repeat offenders. Beeson’s performance supplies the volatile center. She delivers each line as though language has become a physical object requiring immediate disposal, shouting near the edge of collapse while retaining enough control to sharpen every phrase. Around her, Woodward’s guitar behaves less like decoration than a damaged power tool, while Oikawa-Dahlson keeps the track planted firmly enough for the electronics to lunge, buck, and misbehave. The video, directed by Beeson, extends the song’s argument into the realm of surveillance horror. “The video takes on the horror of surveillance,” says Beeson. “While using a lot of throwback technology, mostly to pay homage to its influence – Peter Christopherson’s video for Ministry’s Over The Shoulder, it very much intends to communicate how more modern technology is being used for violence against our communities and humanity as a whole. It fits with the concept of ANIMAL: whether the nature is sexual or simply a desire to exist, we deserve to have freedom and we must take that freedom back.” Watch the video for Animal below: That conviction also drives RESISTANCE, the six-track EP arriving September 4 through Dais Records. Written amid fires, displacement, ICE raids, and the grinding obscenity of late-stage capitalism, the record channels anger toward collective action rather than private despair. “Resistance, less of an idea, more of an absolute action that has to be taken,” asserts Beeson. ANIMAL makes that action feel immediate, physical, and dangerously enjoyable. Revolution may remain poorly organized, but PUREST FORM have at least supplied it with a better bassline. Listen to ANIMAL below and order the single here. items.body: Once all the papers get signed We lift you up on discount price You just have to make this sacrifice Every false prophet and messiah begins by telling the frightened that they have been chosen. The voice offers clarity, belonging, and the promise of a perfected self; only later come the contract, the price, and the surrender of everything that made the convert difficult to own. On Sacrifice, Southeast London industrial post-punk project The Pixel Rain sends that transaction through the age of algorithmic gurus, where charisma can pass for truth and transformation becomes a product. Sacrifice is the second single and opening track from The Pixel Rain’s forthcoming debut album, A Sense of Danger, currently scheduled for release in late October. Following Last, the song introduces the album’s post-apocalyptic frame through a society governed by power, authority, consumerism, and technological control. Sacrifice moves through a cyberpunk dream of deep bass, Kraftwerkian retro-computer pulses, and synth leads glowing with the sterile polish of a showroom terminal. Áron Siegler’s dusky voice maintains a close, controlled pressure throughout the verses, then surges through the chorus’s “So trust me,” landing somewhere between Brian Molko, Trent Reznor, and Paul Banks. Driving rhythms and industrial textures keep the track pushing ahead as the promise at its center grows steadily more predatory. The lyrics borrow the soothing vocabulary of cults, motivational seminars, and influencer culture. The prophet addresses his followers as “children,” while the parenthetical responses—“We’ll hold you” and “You know we leave no one behind”—resemble scripted affirmations designed to smother suspicion. A promise to remove self-doubt soon becomes permission to remove the self, with salvation reduced to paperwork, discount pricing, and the command, “You have to sell yourself tonight.” The final verse reveals what this digital saviour has wanted all along. “I prey on the void inside” turns an apparent confession of faith into an admission of appetite, before the closing line—“So we can eat you alive”—strips the sales pitch of its remaining benevolence. Siegler describes the false prophet behind the song: “‘Sacrifice’ started with the idea of modern-day false messiahs and how easily charisma can be mistaken for truth. As online platforms continue to blur the line between genuine guidance and performance, I found myself drawn to the psychology behind people who build influence by promising transformation. That idea felt like the perfect companion to the track’s cold, mechanical, electronic atmosphere.” The song’s science-fiction setting preceded its arrangement: “Like many of my songs, ‘Sacrifice’ started with a visual idea rather than a musical one. I was inspired by the worlds of Neuromancer and Cyberpunk 2077, and that atmosphere naturally led to a synth-heavy sound. From there, I mixed melodic influences from bands like Depeche Mode and Muse with the industrial pulse and textures of Nine Inch Nails and Ministry.” Created by Ádám Molnár, the accompanying lyric visualizer treats the viewer’s screen as the target of a computer virus. A digitized version of Siegler’s head becomes the infection’s persuasive face, addressing the viewer as the virtual machinery draws them further into its illusion. The polished interface connects the song’s false promises to the screens through which those promises now spread. Watch the visualizer for Sacrifice below: Sacrifice by The Pixel Rain is out via Bandcamp, Spotify, and all major digital platforms. A Sense of Danger is currently scheduled for release in late October. Listen to Sacrifice below, and order the single here. Sacrifice by The Pixel Rain Founded by Hungarian-born vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Áron Siegler, The Pixel Rain took shape within Southeast London’s underground and released a self-titled debut EP in 2023. Drawing from industrial rock, post-punk, synth-pop, and electronic music, Siegler balances guitar-led songwriting with layered production, dark atmospheres, and sharply defined melodies. A Sense of Danger extends that approach across songs concerned with power, authority, consumerism, and social unease, viewed through post-apocalyptic imagery and cold electronic machinery. items.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees released their third studio album, “Kaleidoscope,” on 1 August 1980 through Polydor Records. The album turns 46 this year. It arrived with a new lineup, drummer Budgie and guitarist John McGeoch replacing Kenny Morris and John McKay, who had abruptly left during the “Join Hands” tour, and it introduced synthesizers and drum machines to the band’s sound for the first time. The band recorded “Kaleidoscope” at Surrey Sound Studios in Leatherhead, the Coach House in Monmouth and Polydor Studios in London between January and May 1980, produced by Nigel Gray with Siouxsie and the Banshees. Siouxsie Sioux handled vocals along with guitar and synthesizer parts, Steven Severin played bass, guitar and synthesizer, and Budgie played drums and percussion; McGeoch contributed guitar, saxophone and keys, and Steve Jones added guitar on several tracks. The eleven-track album runs “Happy House,” “Tenant,” “Trophy,” “Hybrid,” “Clockface,” “Lunar Camel,” “Christine,” “Desert Kisses,” “Red Light,” “Paradise Place” and “Skin,” and was preceded by the singles “Happy House” and “Christine.” “Kaleidoscope” reached number 5 on the UK Albums Chart, the band’s highest chart position, and was later certified silver by the BPI. It streams on Spotify. About Siouxsie and the Banshees Siouxsie and the Banshees formed in London in 1976, when vocalist Siouxsie Sioux and bassist Steven Severin, part of the group of Sex Pistols followers known as the Bromley Contingent, put together an impromptu band to fill a slot at the 100 Club Punk Festival on 20 September 1976, playing a 20-minute improvisation with Marco Pirroni on guitar and Sid Vicious on drums. A settled lineup formed around Siouxsie, Severin, guitarist John McKay and drummer Kenny Morris, and Polydor signed the band in June 1978 after the single “Hong Kong Garden” reached the UK top ten. The band’s debut album, “The Scream,” followed on 13 November 1978, and “Join Hands” arrived in 1979. Two days into the tour for “Join Hands,” McKay and Morris abruptly left the band, and Siouxsie and the Banshees regrouped around new guitarist John McGeoch, formerly of Magazine, and new drummer Budgie, formerly of the Slits. This lineup of Siouxsie, Severin, McGeoch and Budgie recorded and released “Kaleidoscope” on 1 August 1980 through Polydor, reaching number 5 on the UK Albums Chart. The band followed it with “Juju” in 1981, which included the single “Spellbound,” and “A Kiss in the Dreamhouse” in 1982. McGeoch left the band in 1982, and the Cure’s Robert Smith joined as guitarist for the “A Kiss in the Dreamhouse” tour and the following two albums; John Valentine Carruthers then took over guitar for “Hyaena” (1984) and “Tinderbox” (1986), and the band released the covers album “Through the Looking Glass” in 1987. Guitarist Jon Klein joined for “Peepshow” (1988), which produced the US breakthrough single “Peek-a-Boo.” After a break during which Siouxsie and Budgie recorded as the Creatures, the band returned with “Superstition” (1991), led by the US hit single “Kiss Them for Me,” and toured as second headliners on the first Lollapalooza. “The Rapture,” produced with John Cale, followed in 1995 before Siouxsie and the Banshees disbanded in April 1996. “Kaleidoscope,” the album that introduced the McGeoch and Budgie-era lineup and the band’s electronic turn, turns 46 this year.

items.body: Suicide Commando, the Belgian electro-industrial project of Johan Van Roy, released its debut album Critical Stage on 1 August 1994 through the German label Off Beat. The CD turns 32 this year. The Suicide Sessions 1 (Critical Stage) by Suicide Commando “Critical Stage” contains 12 tracks, all written and performed by Van Roy, recorded and mixed by Eric Van Wonterghem at E.M.P.-studio. Cover design and layout came from Beyond > Mixed Data and Koen Cant. Track ten, “Where Do We Go From Here?”, carries voice and lyrics by Dirk Ivens, known from Dive, The Klinik and Absolute Body Control. Off Beat, a division of the German company Westcom, distributed the album through SPV GmbH. The original CD is out of print. The album can be streamed today via Bandcamp as part of “The Suicide Sessions 1 (Critical Stage)”, a 2011 reissue that restores the original twelve tracks alongside eleven bonus recordings. Out Of Line reissued “Critical Stage” separately on limited red and yellow vinyl in 2025. About Suicide Commando Johan Van Roy started experimenting with electronic music in Belgium in 1986 under the name Suicide Commando. His first tape followed two years later, and a track from it appeared on the vinyl compilation “Electronic.” After several more self-released tapes, Off Beat signed Van Roy, and Suicide Commando’s debut album, “Critical Stage,” followed in 1994. A second album, “Stored Images,” arrived in 1995 and included “See You in Hell.” In 1996, Van Roy marked the project’s tenth anniversary with the compilation “Contamination.” “Construct-Destruct” and its companion release “Reconstruction” followed in 1998, carrying the club tracks “Desire” and “Better Off Dead.” Van Roy co-founded the label Dependent in 1999. Suicide Commando’s next studio album, “Mindstrip” (2000), reached number one on the German Alternative Charts and was licensed for North America by Metropolis Records. Dependent also released the singles “Hellraiser” and “Comatose Delusion,” the EP “Love Breeds Suicide,” and the 2002 compilation “Anthology.” The 2003 album “Axis of Evil” was voted album of the year by the Deutsche Alternative Charts. “Bind, Torture, Kill” followed in 2006, preceded by the single “Godsend + Menschenfresser,” and reached number one on the DAC albums chart. Suicide Commando marked its 20th anniversary in 2007 with the “X20” boxset, including a remix disc, a “best of” disc, the “Fuck You Bitch” EP and the project’s first live DVD. In 2009, Van Roy signed with the German label Out Of Line, starting with the 7″ “Severed Head / Until We Die.” The album “Implements of Hell” followed in 2010, again licensed to Metropolis Records in the US. In 2011, Suicide Commando reissued its first three studio albums, “Critical Stage,” “Stored Images” and “Construct-Destruct,” as the six-CD box “The Suicide Sessions,” each remastered and paired with a disc of bonus and previously unreleased material. “When Evil Speaks” followed in 2013, led by the single “Attention Whore” and reaching number 47 on the German Media Control Charts. “Forest of the Impaled” (2017) included “The Pain That You Like,” a single featuring Jean-Luc De Meyer of Front 242 as guest vocalist, and reached number 28 on the same chart. Suicide Commando released the album “Goddestruktor” in 2022. For live shows, Van Roy performs alongside Torben Schmidt on keyboards and Mario Vaerewijck on drums. “Critical Stage,” the album that started the project’s studio discography, turns 32 on 1 August.

items.body: Los Angeles dance-punk trio Purest Form has signed to Dais Records. The label will release the band’s second EP, “RESISTANCE”, on September 4, 2026, and Purest Form has shared a video for the opening track, “Animal.” Purest Form is Story Beeson (vocals), Madi Woodward (guitar, programming) and Riley Oikawa-Dahlson (bass). The trio formed in Los Angeles in 2023 and draws on members’ backgrounds in hardcore bands alongside a shared interest in industrial and techno production. RESISTANCE by Purest Form “RESISTANCE” runs six tracks: “Animal,” “Break,” “Beyond Terror,” “More,” “Bass Resistance” and “Breathe.” The EP closes with a cover of The Prodigy’s “Breathe,” a song the band has performed live. Recording took place across 2025 with longtime collaborator and producer Andrew Oswald. The release is confirmed on CD and 12″ vinyl, including a black smoke vinyl variant. Video for ‘Animal’ addresses surveillance technology Beeson directed the video for “Animal,” the EP’s opening track. The video uses older recording technology to address the use of modern surveillance tools against communities. Woodward describes the direction behind “RESISTANCE” as a deliberate widening of the band’s sound: “We decided to just take it to the next level with this one. It’s like a unification of all the music that we love and feel. And it makes sense to us. If it sounds good, we don’t care where it comes from.” Beeson connects the EP to events in Los Angeles during 2025: “The nature and actions of our country are overwhelming, I can’t get away from the feeling of ‘what can we do to resist this at all costs?’ We have very radical fantasies across the board, making music that isn’t talking about what’s happening right now just feels unimportant to us.” About Purest Form Purest Form formed in Los Angeles in 2023, when Woodward and Beeson met while working at an independent venue in the city and bonded over a shared interest in underground music. Beeson also performs with Choking on Ash and Vacant Future, Woodward with Fury and Object of Affection, and Oikawa-Dahlson with Roman Candles and Pocketknife. The band released a self-titled debut EP in 2024, a set built around heavy, distorted guitar and programmed percussion. “RESISTANCE,” out September 4, 2026, is Purest Form’s second EP and its first release for Dais Records, recorded during 2025 with producer Andrew Oswald and led by the single “Animal.”

items.body: Chicago post-punk trio French Police has signed to Interscope Records. The band’s first release for the label is the digital double single “Reptile” and “Japan,” released July 30, 2026, each accompanied by an official video produced by Someoddpilot Studios and directed by Chris Eichenseer. French Police is Brian Flores (vocals, guitar), Manny Herrera (lead guitar) and Rolando Donjuan (bass). The Interscope signing follows the band’s earlier releases through the independent label Icy Cold Records, including the 2020 album “Haunted Castle,” reviewed by Side-Line, and 2025 limited European vinyl editions of “Bully” and “Haunted Castle.” Video for ‘Japan’ The second track, “Japan,” has its own official video, also produced by Someoddpilot Studios and directed by Eichenseer. “Reptile / Japan” is available to stream on Spotify. Tour dates for French Police French Police will tour North America in support of the Interscope signing from September through October 2026. About French Police French Police formed in Chicago in 2018, led by vocalist and guitarist Brian Flores following the end of his earlier band, Karma Wears White Ties, which he ran with his brother Jesse Flores from 2012 to 2018. The current lineup adds lead guitarist Manny Herrera and bassist Rolando Donjuan. The band released a self-titled debut album in 2019, followed by “Haunted Castle” in 2020 and “BLEU” in 2023, all through the independent label Icy Cold Records. The full-length “Bully” followed in January 2024; Side-Line covered its limited European vinyl edition, released alongside a “Haunted Castle” vinyl edition, in 2025. French Police signed to Interscope Records in 2026, releasing the double single “Reptile / Japan” on July 30 as its first output for the label, backed by a North American tour running September through October 2026.

items.body: Dallas, Texas darkwave duo NITE has released a video for “Cries for Help,” the title track from their 2024 EP, ahead of a run of North American, UK and Czech tour dates stretching from August through November 2026. Cries For Help by Nite NITE is the project of twin brothers Myles Mendes and Kyle Mendes, born in Winnipeg, Canada and based in Dallas. The duo perform live with drummer Phil Helms. Their sound mixes darkwave, post-punk and synth-pop elements with dual harmonized vocals. Video for ‘Cries for Help’ The video for “Cries for Help” accompanies the closing single from NITE’s six-track EP of the same name, released August 26, 2024 on Nite’s Bandcamp. The EP also includes “All Your Pain,” “Our Light Will Never Die,” “Oblivion (My Obsession),” “Have Mercy” and “Price For Heaven.” Tour dates for NITE NITE’s 2026 touring schedule spans three legs: a UK/Czech run, a South/East Coast and Midwest run with support act Echos, and a West Coast run with support act Julien-K, followed by Texas dates. About NITE NITE formed in Dallas, Texas around producers and twin brothers Myles Mendes and Kyle Mendes, who were born in Winnipeg, Canada. The duo self-released their debut album, “I Am Not Afraid,” in 2014. They signed to Cleopatra Records and released “Reborn” on July 28, 2017, featuring the song “Dreamer,” followed by “Sleepless” in 2020, also through Cleopatra Records. NITE released the six-track EP “Cries For Help” on August 26, 2024, and followed it with their fifth full-length, self-titled album “NITE,” on October 21, 2025, issued in limited vinyl and CD quantities. The band performs live with drummer Phil Helms and has toured with acts including The New Division, Small Black, A Flock of Seagulls, Berlin and Midge Ure. NITE’s current tour, supporting the video for “Cries for Help,” runs from July through November 2026 across the US, UK and Czech Republic.

items.body: Hungarian artist István Gazdag has built a solid reputation within the EBM scene through his primary project, First Aid 4 Souls. A true workaholic, he is also active with side projects such as First Aid Tech. Two years ago, he released the outstanding debut album “Tech Under Your Skin” under this moniker. That impressive work is now followed by a new release featuring—once again—no fewer than 22 tracks. The influences remain largely unchanged. István Gazdag continues to experiment freely with a wide range of styles, moving from EBM—inevitably inviting comparisons to Front Line Assembly—to Tribal and Psy-Trance elements that occasionally evoke the spirit of Juno Reactor. Acid sequences emerge throughout the album, while guitar passages provide yet another subtle nod to the latter’s signature sound. Despite these obvious influences, First Aid Tech never comes across as derivative. Instead, the music feels like a seamless fusion of the various styles this sound guru effortlessly combines. There are no vocals, although carefully selected samples add extra depth and variety. The tracks frequently exude a menacing atmosphere that perfectly complements the album’s dark overall mood. Once again, Gazdag delivers a meticulously crafted production that merges boundless creativity with sophisticated, high-tech production values. To my ears, this new opus plays like the imaginary soundtrack to a “Matrix”-esque film. Above all, however, it stands as a brilliant, elaborate, and deeply immersive obscure Electro production. (Rating:8½). Listen to “Play My Game”: Play My Game by First Aid Tech About First Aid Tech First Aid Tech is a project of Hungarian electronic musician István Gazdag, who is also the driving force behind First Aid 4 Souls and Stahlgeist. First Aid 4 Souls, active since 2007, is known for its blend of industrial, EBM, dark ambient, trance, and new wave, often featuring guest vocalists. Stahlgeist deals in EBM that recalls the early years of Front Line Assembly and Wumpscut. Gazdag has performed and DJed under the First Aid Tech moniker for years, but the project’s first official release, a self-titled techno body EP featuring 4 tracks and 4 bonus remixes, only appeared on Alfa Matrix on December 4, 2023. The debut album, “Tech Under Your Skin,” followed on October 17, 2024. In a Side-Line interview, Gazdag described First Aid Tech’s sound DNA as rooted in 90s electronic music, citing Cabaret Voltaire, Orbital, Yello, Juno Reactor, LFO, Underworld, Empirion, and Future Sound Of London as reference points. The project now returns with its second full-length, “Back To Agartha.”

items.body: ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■1. 愛着理論の基礎━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━愛着理論はイギリスの精神科医ジョン・ボウルビィが提唱し、後にメアリー・エインスワースが「ストレンジ・シチュエーション法」という実験で発展させた理論です。乳幼児が養育者との間に「安全基地」を築けるかどうかが、その後の対人関係の土台になるという考え方です。エインスワースの実験では、乳児の反応から「安定型」「不安型(アンビバレント型)」「回避型」の3分類が生まれ、後にメアリー・メインらが「無秩序・無方向型(disorganized)」を追加し、現在の4分類の原型ができました。出典: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_attachment_theory成人の恋愛関係にこの理論を応用したのは、シンシア・ハザンとフィリップ・シェイバーによる1987年の研究で、「安心型」「不安型」「回避型」という枠組みが恋愛心理学に持ち込まれました。出典: https://tfp-group.co.jp/love-bond/column/kaihitype-koi現在、成人の愛着スタイルを測る学術的な尺度としては「ECR(Experiences in Close Relationships)」やその改訂版「ECR-R」、Fraleyらによる「ECR-RS」などがあり、「不安」と「回避」という2軸で4タイプに分類する方式が主流です。出典: https://www.simplypsychology.org/dismissive-avoidant-attachment-style-signs-how-to-heal.html━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■2. 「回避型」の特徴━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━複数の情報源に共通して挙げられている特徴をまとめると、以下のようになります。・一人の時間を強く好み、群れることを避ける・人に頼ることも、頼られることも苦手・感情表現が乏しく、自分の感情そのものに気づきにくい・関係が深まりそうになると自分から距離を置く、または関係を終わらせる・恋愛で好意を向けられると急に冷たくなる、連絡を絶つ・表面的には自立していて冷静に見えるが、内面では孤独感や空虚感を抱えている・過去や自分の感情に向き合うことを頑なに避ける・子ども時代の記憶があいまいなことが多い出典: https://note.com/joyous_panda771/n/ndb85f8cdcc13出典: https://psychotherapy.jp/avoidant-attachment-seven-characteristics-relationship-problems/出典: https://sanyokai-clinic.com/kokoro/8045/出典: https://katsushikabashi.jp/article/avoidant-attachment-style/岡田尊司氏の著書「回避性愛着障害」では、感情を強く揺さぶられる写真を一瞬見せて理解するまでの時間を計測する実験が紹介されており、回避型の人は感情を喚起する写真の理解に時間がかかる(=感情への反応が鈍い)という結果が示されています。この傾向は自然の風景や無機物の写真には見られなかったとされています。出典: https://coconala.com/blogs/2307087/319522(岡田尊司「愛着障害~子供時代を引きずる人々~」からの引用紹介)━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■3. 英語圏での分類：dismissive-avoidant(拒絶回避型)━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━英語圏では回避型は主に「dismissive-avoidant(拒絶回避型)」と呼ばれ、以下のような特徴が整理されています。・極端な自己完結性・独立性・親密になることへの抵抗、コミットメントの回避・表面的な会話で終わらせようとする傾向・長期的な関係より短期的・カジュアルな関係を好む傾向があるという研究結果もある・パートナーへの依存(interpersonal dependence)や信頼のスコアが低い・失恋時の苦痛が(特に男性で)比較的軽いという研究結果もある出典: https://www.simplypsychology.org/dismissive-avoidant-attachment-style-signs-how-to-heal.html出典: https://www.rula.com/blog/dismissive-avoidant-attachment/出典: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4873099/(Machiavellianism and Adult Attachment研究)「Dismissive」は依存を弱さと捉える傾向があり、実際には人間関係を求めていないわけではなく、期待して裏切られることを恐れて自分から距離を作っている、という解釈がCharlie Healthの記事で紹介されています。出典: https://www.charliehealth.com/post/dismissive-avoidant-attachment-style-what-you-need-to-know━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■4. 「恐れ・回避型」(fearful-avoidant / disorganized)との違い━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━回避型(dismissive-avoidant)と混同されやすいのが「恐れ・回避型(fearful-avoidant)」です。両者は「距離を取る」という表面上の行動は似ていますが、内的な動機がまったく異なります。・回避型(dismissive)：親密さを「不要」「わずらわしい」と感じ、自己完結によって心の安定を保つ。感情を意図的に抑え込む「非活性化」が基本戦略・恐れ・回避型(fearful)：親密さを強く求めながら同時に強い恐怖も感じ、「近づきたいのに怖い」という内的な葛藤(push-pull)を抱える。虐待的・混沌とした養育環境から形成されやすいとされる出典: https://www.attachmentproject.com/blog/fearful-avoidant-vs-dismissive-avoidant/出典: https://freudly.ai/blog/fearful-avoidant-vs-dismissive-avoidant/出典: https://missionconnectionhealthcare.com/mental-health/attachment-disorder/dismissive-avoidant-vs-fearful-avoidant/なお、「無秩序型(disorganized)=恐れ・回避型」という等式は社会心理学者の間で異論もあり、無秩序な愛着システムが必ずしも恐れ・回避型と一致するわけではないという指摘もあります。出典: https://www.attachmentproject.com/blog/fearful-avoidant-vs-dismissive-avoidant/Chateau Recoveryの記事によれば、恐れ・回避型は一般人口の約7%に見られるとされていますが、臨床・オンラインの自己選択サンプルでは特に18~24歳でより高い割合が報告されているとのことです。出典: https://www.chateaurecovery.com/avoidant-dismissive-attachment-style━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■5. 形成の背景・原因━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━複数のソースで共通して挙げられている要因は以下の通りです。・養育者が子どもの感情的なニーズに応答しない、または感情表現を軽んじる/拒否する・ネグレクト(育児放棄)や情緒的に距離のある養育・「自立を促す」という名目で実際には世話を怠る養育方針・親との死別・離婚などによる養育者の喪失体験・親自身が愛着に問題を抱えており、世代を超えて連鎖する出典: https://tfp-group.co.jp/love-bond/column/kaihitype-koi出典: https://sanyokai-clinic.com/kokoro/8045/出典: https://diamond.jp/articles/-/329448?page=2ダイヤモンド・オンラインの記事では、回避型に育つ子どもの親は「世話をしないことで自立心を養っている」という言い訳をしがちだが、実際には子どもは心の奥で「誰かが距離を縮めてくること」への強い不安を抱えたまま育つ可能性があると指摘されています。また、養育者との精神的つながりの薄さから「ミラーリング(感情の映し返し)」の機会を失い、感情の言語化能力が育ちにくいことも述べられています。出典: https://diamond.jp/articles/-/329448?page=2━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■6. 医学的な位置づけ:「愛着障害」という言葉の注意点━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ここは特に誤解が多いポイントです。「回避型愛着障害」という呼び方が広く使われていますが、DSM-5(米国精神医学会の診断基準)で正式に「障害」として定義されているのは以下の2つのみです。・反応性アタッチメント障害(反応性愛着障害):養育者への安らぎを求めない、感情表現が乏しいなど。乳児~就学前の子どもが対象で、著しいネグレクトや虐待、養育者の頻繁な交代が診断の必須要件・脱抑制型対人交流障害:見知らぬ大人にも過度になれなれしく接する出典: https://kurumi.makecare.co.jp/column/attachment-disorder-diagnostic-4style/出典: https://www.e-heartclinic.com/kokoro-info/special/motion_7.htmlいずれも「臨床場面ではまれにしか診断されない」「重度のネグレクトを受けた子どものうち10%未満にしか生じない」とされる、稀な小児期の診断です。出典: https://mental-cocoromi-cl.jp/blog/%E3%80%8E%E5%8F%8D%E5%BF%9C%E6%80%A7%E6%84%9B%E7%9D%80%E9%9A%9C%E5%AE%B3%E3%81%A8%E8%84%B1%E6%8A%91%E5%88%B6%E5%9E%8B%E5%AF%BE%E4%BA%BA%E4%BA%A4%E6%B5%81%E9%9A%9C%E5%AE%B3%E3%80%8F%E3%81%AE%E6%9C%80-2つまり、SNSや自己分析でよく使われる「回避型愛着障害」「不安型愛着障害」といった言葉は、正式な精神医学的診断名ではなく、成人の愛着"スタイル"(パーソナリティ傾向に近い概念)を指す通称です。就労支援会社Kaienのコラムでは、大人が「愛着障害」を自認するケースが近年増えている一方、実際に診断名として使われることは稀であり、位置づけとしてはアダルトチルドレンやHSPに近いという指摘がなされています。重要なのは「今の生きづらさが何であるか」よりも「今の生きづらさをどう解消していくか」であるとも述べられています。出典: https://www.kaien-lab.com/useful/3-traits/attachment-disorder/━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■7. 恋愛関係における回避型:「非活性化戦略」━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━成人の愛着スタイルを一般に広めた代表的な書籍が、精神科医エイミー・レヴィンと心理学者レイチェル・ヘラーによる「Attached(邦題:異性の心を上手に透視する方法/愛着障害への理解を広めた一冊として頻繁に引用される)」です。同書では回避型の人が親密さを避けるために使う「非活性化戦略(deactivating strategies)」として、以下のようなものが挙げられています。・パートナーの小さな欠点にこだわり、それを理由に距離を置く・「今はコミットする準備ができていない」と言いながら関係自体は長く続ける・元恋人を理想化して、今のパートナーと比較する「ファントム・エックス」・関係をあいまいなまま定義しないでおく・物理的な距離を保つ、秘密を持つ出典: パートナーや周囲の人ができるサポート━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━回避型本人だけでなく、周囲の人がどう接するかも克服のプロセスに影響します。・いきなり感情的な話題に踏み込まず、まずは論理的・具体的な会話から信頼関係を築く・共通の活動(例:週末どこに行くか一緒に決める)など、ストレスの少ない接点を作る・相手にとっての「安全基地」になる:安定した態度を保ち、批判的な言動を避ける・期待した反応がすぐに返ってこないことを想定し、寛容な態度で接する・相手の関心ごとに合わせて会話をすることで、信頼関係を築きやすくなる出典: https://atsu.theletter.jp/posts/02c2faa0-db54-11ee-af9e-ade4fb3034e5出典: https://mental.kashiwa-ekimae.com/34360/出典: https://tayama-counseling-office.com/%E5%9B%9E%E9%81%BF%E4%BE%9D%E5%AD%98%E3%83%BB%E5%9B%9E%E9%81%BF%E5%9E%8B%E6%84%9B%E7%9D%80%E3%82%B9%E3%82%BF%E3%82%A4%E3%83%AB%E3%81%AE%E4%BA%BA%E3%81%A8%E3%81%AE%E4%BB%98%E3%81%8D%E5%90%88%E3%81%84/学術研究でも、ポジティブな関係経験そのものが回避型愛着傾向を持つ人に恩恵をもたらすことが示されており、良い関係経験を重ねること自体が回避傾向を和らげる方向に働く可能性が示唆されています(Stanton, Campbell, & Pink, 2017, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology)。出典: https://light-clinic.com/what-is-avoidant-behavior/━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■6. 注意点・現実的な見通し━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━・「治す」というより「傾向を緩める」というイメージの方が実態に近いとされています。回避型は障害というより関係性のパターンであり、不安やトラウマ歴と併存することはあっても、それ自体が精神疾患ではないという立場を取る専門家もいます出典: https://texascip.com/overcoming-avoidant-attachment-with-therapy/・変化は直線的ではなく、「気づき→実践→後退→また気づく」というらせん状のプロセスであると複数のセラピストが述べています出典: https://psychology4u.net/psychology/how-to-heal-an-avoidant-attachment-style-a-psychology-based-guide/・特に恐れ・回避型の場合は、神経系の調整(グラウンディングなど)により重点を置く必要があるとされ、単純な「距離を縮める練習」だけでは不十分な場合があります出典: https://psychology4u.net/psychology/how-to-heal-an-avoidant-attachment-style-a-psychology-based-guide/・セルフヘルプでの取り組みが難しいと感じる場合、専門的な心理療法(個人・カップルどちらも)が選択肢として推奨されています出典: https://www.brentwoodtherapycollective.com/blog/how-to-heal-an-avoidant-attachment-style-steps-to-build-secure-relationships━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■まとめ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━回避型愛着の克服については、日本語圏では岡田尊司氏の「子ども心を取り戻す」「他者を受け入れる」「自分が自分の親になる」という3段階の枠組みが広く参照されています。一方、欧米の心理療法分野ではEFT・CBT・IFS・ソマティックセラピー・EMDRなど複数のエビデンスベースの手法が併用され、「洞察だけでなく、安全な経験の反復によって変わる」という点が共通して強調されています。続きをみる

items.excerpt: ■ 基本プロフィール本名リチャード・アルパート（Richard Alpert）。1931年4月6日、マサチューセッツ州ニュートンの裕福なユダヤ系家庭に誕生。父ジョージ・アルパートはボストンで有力な弁護士で、ニューヨーク・ニューヘブン・アンド・ハートフォード鉄道の社長を務め、ブランダイス大学とアルバート・アインシュタイン医学校の創立者の一人でもあった大物。3人兄弟の末っ子で、幼少期は「家族のマスコット」的存在として愛されて育つ。タフツ大学で学士号、ウェズリアン大学で修士号を取得後、1957年にスタンフォード大学で心理学博士号を取得（博士論文のテーマは「達成不安」）。その後ハーバード大学で心理学の助教授となり、社会関係学部・心理学部・大学院教育学部・保健サービス部門を渡り歩くエリート学者だった。メルセデスを乗り回し、カリブ海に別荘を持ち、自家用飛行機まで所有していたという。参照：https://www.inc.com/minda-zetlin/ram-dass-influenced-steve-jobs-be-here-now.html■ ハーバード時代とティモシー・リアリーとのサイケデリ
items.body: ■ 基本プロフィール本名リチャード・アルパート（Richard Alpert）。1931年4月6日、マサチューセッツ州ニュートンの裕福なユダヤ系家庭に誕生。父ジョージ・アルパートはボストンで有力な弁護士で、ニューヨーク・ニューヘブン・アンド・ハートフォード鉄道の社長を務め、ブランダイス大学とアルバート・アインシュタイン医学校の創立者の一人でもあった大物。3人兄弟の末っ子で、幼少期は「家族のマスコット」的存在として愛されて育つ。タフツ大学で学士号、ウェズリアン大学で修士号を取得後、1957年にスタンフォード大学で心理学博士号を取得（博士論文のテーマは「達成不安」）。その後ハーバード大学で心理学の助教授となり、社会関係学部・心理学部・大学院教育学部・保健サービス部門を渡り歩くエリート学者だった。メルセデスを乗り回し、カリブ海に別荘を持ち、自家用飛行機まで所有していたという。参照：https://www.inc.com/minda-zetlin/ram-dass-influenced-steve-jobs-be-here-now.html■ ハーバード時代とティモシー・リアリーとのサイケデリック研究1958年からハーバードで教え始め、1961年にはハーバード心理学部の同僚ティモシー・リアリーと出会う。二人はシロシビン（マジックマッシュルーム由来）やLSDを用いた意識研究「ハーバード・シロシビン・プロジェクト」に没頭し、自らも被験者として服用。ジャズミュージシャン、物理学者、哲学者、聖職者、麻薬常用者、大学院生など多様な被験者に薬物を投与し、体験後にアンケートを取るという手法を取った。1962年にはリアリーと共に非営利団体「国際内的自由連盟（IFIF）」をケンブリッジで共同設立し、宗教的文脈での向精神薬使用を研究。この研究は『チベット死者の書』を下敷きにした共著『The Psychedelic Experience』（リアリー、ラルフ・メツナーと共著）や『LSD』（シドニー・コーエン、ローレンス・シラーと共著）という書籍を生んだが、あまりに物議を醸したため、1963年、大学院生にもシロシビンを与えたことなどを理由にハーバードを解雇される（リアリーも無断で講義を休んだこと等を理由に同時解雇）。なお、リアリーの息子ジャック（当時15歳）を「誘惑しようとした」との告発もアルパートの死亡記事（NYT）に記されている。参照：https://www.ramdass.org/about-ram-dass/参照：https://matthewremski.com/wordpress/quotes-from-ram-dass-that-fit-the-pattern-of-spiritualizing-sexual-abuse-in-yoga/■ インドへの旅とニーム・カロリ・ババとの出会い1967年、アルパートはインドへ。旅の途中でネパールにて、アメリカ人の精神探求者バガヴァン・ダス（本名カーミット・マイケル・リッグス）と出会い、裸足で寺院を巡りながらマントラやアーサナ、数珠の使い方などの手ほどきを受ける。数ヶ月後、バガヴァン・ダスに導かれ、カインチ・アシュラムでヒンドゥー教の導師ニーム・カロリ・ババ（西洋では「マハラジ・ジ」として知られる）に出会う。伝説的なエピソードとして、アルパートが持参した大量のLSDをマハラジ・ジに服用させたところ、何の効果も表れなかった（少なくともアルパート自身はそう語っている）という逸話がある。マハラジ・ジはアルパートに「ラム・ダス（神の下僕）」という名を授け、これが彼の以後の人生を決定づけた。1968年に帰国。参照：https://allthatsinteresting.com/ram-dass参照：https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ram-Dass■ 『Be Here Now』（1971年）― ヒッピー世代のバイブル帰国後、心理学から瞑想やヨガ、東洋思想の伝道者へと転身。1971年に出版した『Be Here Now（ビー・ヒア・ナウ／心の扉をひらく本）』は自伝的要素とヒンドゥー教・仏教思想を融合させた内容で、カウンターカルチャー世代の聖典的存在となった。タイトルの「Be Here Now」は、旅の途中でバガヴァン・ダスが彼に繰り返しかけた言葉「過去のことは考えるな、ただ今ここにいろ」に由来するとされる。日本語版は平河出版社より刊行、訳者は上野圭一・吉福伸逸・スワミ・プレム・プラブッダ。参照：https://hirakawa-shuppan.co.jp/pickup/%E3%83%93%E3%83%BC%E3%83%BB%E3%83%92%E3%82%A2%E3%83%BB%E3%83%8A%E3%82%A6/参照：https://shopping.bookoff.co.jp/used/0015279360■ スティーブ・ジョブズとの関係『Be Here Now』はアップル創業者スティーブ・ジョブズの愛読書として広く知られる。1972年、リード大学に入学したばかりのジョブズはLSDを試しながら精神世界の本を読み漁っており、この本に強い影響を受けた。ジョブズ自身「profound（深遠）だった。自分や多くの友人を変容させた」と語ったと伝記作家ウォルター・アイザックソンの著作に記されている。ジョブズがインドへ渡った動機の一つも、この本の影響とされる。ラム・ダスはジョブズのほか、ザッカーバーグやラリー・ペイジなど後のIT業界のキーパーソンにも影響を与えたと言われる。参照：https://theceolibrary.com/be-here-now-636.html参照：https://tocana.jp/2019/12/post_134639_entry.html■ 慈善・社会活動1974年、非営利団体「ハヌマーン・ファウンデーション」を設立。傘下で刑務所を「僧院」に見立てて受刑者に瞑想を教える「プリズン・アシュラム・プロジェクト」（現ヒューマン・カインドネス・ファウンデーション、ボー＆シータ・ロゾフ夫妻が主導）や、死にゆく人々への意識的な向き合い方を支援する「ダイイング・プロジェクト」（スティーブン・レヴァインと構想、後にデイル・ボーグラムが主導する「Living/Dying Project」に発展）を展開。1978年には公衆衛生の専門家ラリー・ブリリアント、活動家ウェイヴィー・グレイヴィーらと共に「セヴァ・ファウンデーション」を共同設立。インド・ネパールなど途上国での失明予防・治療事業を行う国際保健団体として現在も活動中。ラム・ダスは著書の印税や講演料の多くをこうした団体に寄付し続けた。参照：https://www.hanumanmaui.org/ram-dass参照：https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seva_Foundation参照：https://www.ihanuman.com/journal/bolozoff/human-kindness-foundation-and-prison-ashram-project■ 1997年の脳卒中と「フィアース・グレイス（Fierce Grace）」1997年2月19日、自宅で一人でいる際に大規模な脳卒中を発症。右半身の麻痺と表出性失語症（言葉を発するのが困難になる症状）が残った。本人はこれを「stroked（打たれた）」と表現し、この経験を「fierce grace（苛烈な恩寵）」と呼んで、老いや死、苦しみへの向き合い方を再び深く見つめ直す契機とした。この時期の回復と変容を描いたドキュメンタリー『Ram Dass, Fierce Grace』（2001年、監督ミッキー・レムル）が制作され、Newsweek誌の2002年ノンフィクション映画トップ5にも選出。脳卒中の体験は著書『Still Here: Embracing Aging, Changing and Dying』（2000年、邦訳『死の処方箋 人はなぜ苦しむのか？』）にまとめられている。なお2004年には命に関わる感染症にも見舞われ、以降は旅行を制限し療養を優先する生活となった。参照：https://www.ramdass.org/about-ram-dass/参照：https://tricycle.org/magazine/ram-dass-fierce-grace-mickey-lemle/参照：https://itvs.org/about/pressroom/press-release/ram-dass-fierce-grace/■ 私生活について1990年代、ラム・ダスは自身のバイセクシュアリティを公言するようになった。ただしラベリングは避け、「バイセクシュアルというのはゲイでもノンゲイでもない、ただの『気づき』なのだ」と語っている。また78歳のとき、24歳当時スタンフォード大学在学中に歴史学専攻の女性カレン・サウムとの関係の中で息子をもうけていたことが判明し、自身が祖父であることも知ることになった。参照：https://en.dharmapedia.net/wiki/Ram_Dass■ 主な著書（年代順）・Identification and Child Rearing（1962、リアリーらと共著）・LSD（1966）・The Psychedelic Experience（1964、リアリー、メツナーと共著）・Be Here Now（1971／邦題『ビー・ヒア・ナウ 心の扉をひらく本』平河出版社）・The Only Dance There Is（1974）・Grist for the Mill（1977、スティーブン・レヴァインと共著）・Journey of Awakening: A Meditator's Guidebook（1978／邦題『覚醒への旅 瞑想者のガイドブック』）・Miracle of Love: Stories of Neem Karoli Baba（1978／邦題『愛という奇蹟 ニーム・カロリ・ババ物語』）・How Can I Help?（ポール・ゴーマンと共著／邦題『ハウ・キャナイ・ヘルプ？ 助け合うときに起こること』）・Compassion in Action: Setting Out on the Path of Service（ミラバイ・ブッシュと共著）・Still Here: Embracing Aging, Changing and Dying（2000／邦題『死の処方箋 人はなぜ苦しむのか？』）・One-Liners: A Mini-Manual for a Spiritual Life・Paths to God: Living the Bhagavad Gita・Polishing the Mirror: How to Live from Your Spiritual Heart（2013、脳卒中後82歳での回顧録的著作）参照：https://insightla.org/teacher/ram-dass/参照：https://www.ramdass.org/about-ram-dass/参照：https://bookmeter.com/authors/283030■ 映像作品・ドキュメンタリー・Ram Dass, Fierce Grace（2001）・Ram Dass – Love Serve Remember（2010、短編）・Dying to Know: Ram Dass & Timothy Leary（2014）・Ram Dass, Going Home（2017、デレク・ペック監督）・Ram Dass, Becoming Nobody（2019、ジェイミー・カトー監督）参照：https://www.ramdass.org/about-ram-dass/■ 晩年とハワイ・マウイ島での生活、そして死晩年はハワイのマウイ島に居を構え、糖尿病性神経障害の痛みを抱えながらも、オンライン講話やポッドキャスト「Here and Now」（Be Here Nowネットワーク内、100話以上配信）を通じて教えを発信し続けた。WIRED誌の記事では、健康上の理由でシロシビンの使用を禁じられていた晩年の様子や、身近で世話をしていた人物との交流が描かれている。2019年12月22日朝、マウイ島の自宅で、愛する人々に囲まれながら安らかに息を引き取った。88歳没。死因は公式には明らかにされていない。公式インスタグラムでは「彼は何千もの人々が、制度化された宗教の内側あるいは外側で、自らの精神的アイデンティティを見出し、あるいは取り戻す手助けをするガイドだった」との追悼メッセージが発表された。参照：https://wired.jp/article/the-day-ram-dass-died/参照：https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/ram-dass-psychedelic-drug-pioneer-author-dies-88-n1106476参照：https://www.cnn.co.jp/usa/35147317.html■ 死後の評価と批判的視点多くの追悼記事はラム・ダスを「聖人」的に描いたが、ヨガ・仏教コミュニティにおける権力関係や性的境界の問題を批判的に検証するライター、マシュー・レムスキーは、ラム・ダスと親密な時間を過ごした女性たちの証言や、前述のリアリーの息子への告発など、「精神的な師弟関係の中でのセクシュアリティの美化・神秘化」という、グル文化に繰り返し見られるパターンへの警鐘を鳴らしている。これは彼の思想的功績と切り離せない、批判的に検討されるべき側面として近年言及されることが増えている。参照：https://matthewremski.com/wordpress/quotes-from-ram-dass-that-fit-the-pattern-of-spiritualizing-sexual-abuse-in-yoga/■ 遺志を継ぐ組織現在は「Love Serve Remember Foundation（LSRF）」が、ニーム・カロリ・ババとラム・ダスの教えを保存・継承する活動を行っている。オンラインコース、ブログ、映画、ポッドキャスト、アーティストとのコラボレーションなどを通じて発信を続けている。参照：https://www.ramdass.org/about-ram-dass/■ 日本での受容日本では知名度は高くないものの、平河出版社を中心に主要著作が翻訳され、ヨガ・瞑想関係者やスピリチュアル系読者の間で読み継がれている。ジョブズの愛読書という文脈で言及されることが多く、村上龍『限りなく透明に近いブルー』などと並べてレビューされることもある。参照：https://note.com/utlyoga/n/n31c9de8714fb参照：https://shopping.bookoff.co.jp/used/0015279360続きをみる
